source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables
source.citation: Toru Koizumi, Toshiki Maekawa, Masanari Mizuno, Maru Kuroki, Tomoaki Tsumura, and Ryota Shioya. 2025. RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables. In Proceedings of the 6th Championship Branch Prediction (CBP 2025), in conjunction with ISCA 2025, June 21, 2025, Tokyo, Japan, pp. 1-6.

summary: The sR (Statistical Corrector Register) component exploits correlations between in-flight architectural/speculative register values and conditional branch outcomes without explicitly tracking data dependencies. It maintains 12-bit compact digests of 65 logical registers tracked via a Tomasulo-like scoreboard. Across 8 banks of registers, usefulness tables (UT) dynamically select the most useful available register digest for each bank at prediction time. Three weight tables (WT) per bank are indexed by combinations of PC and the selected digest to produce partial prediction sums. The per-bank contribution is gated and scaled by x2.5 if useful (or x0 if not useful or unavailable), and all eight bank outputs are summed to yield the sR component prediction input to the SC perceptron adder. Stale digests are pruned via an 8-bit decay counter expiring after 256 decoded instructions.

state.name: Register Tracking Table (Tomasulo-like Scoreboard)
state.organization: Direct-mapped array of 65 entries corresponding to logical registers (R0-R64, covering integer, floating-point, and condition flags)
state.entry_format: valid: 1 bit, payload: 14 bits (holds 14-bit in-flight ROB tag when valid=0, or 12-bit register value digest when valid=1), decay_ctr: 8 bits
state.indexing: Directly indexed by logical register index (0 to 64)

state.name: Usefulness Weight Tables (UT)
state.organization: 8 banks; each bank contains 3 tables (UT0, UT1, UT2) of 8 entries each. Bank 0 tracks 9 registers (R0, R8, ..., R64); Banks 1-7 track 8 registers each (e.g., Bank i tracks logical registers where reg_id % 8 == i). Each entry contains a vector of 6-bit signed usefulness weights for all registers in that bank.
state.entry_format: Bank 0: 9 x 6-bit signed weights (54 bits/entry); Banks 1-7: 8 x 6-bit signed weights (48 bits/entry)
state.indexing: Indexed by skewed PC hash functions into 8-entry tables: index_UTk = Hash_k(PC) % 8 for k in {0, 1, 2}

state.name: Prediction Weight Tables (WT)
state.organization: 8 banks; each bank contains 3 tables with geometric entry capacities: WT0 (512 entries), WT1 (256 entries), WT2 (128 entries). Each entry stores one 6-bit signed saturating weight.
state.indexing: Indexed by hashes of branch PC and the selected 12-bit register digest: index_WT0 = Hash0(PC, digest) % 512, index_WT1 = Hash1(PC, digest) % 256, index_WT2 = Hash2(PC, digest) % 128

algorithms.name: Digest Generation
algorithms.trigger: Instruction execution complete / writeback (when functional execution produces a register value)
algorithms.notes: Counts for leading/trailing bits cap at 63 to fit in 6-bit fields. FP digests place format slices starting at bit position 3, leaving bits [2:0] zero.

algorithms.name: Register Scoreboard Update and Aging
algorithms.trigger: Decode stage, Execution completion, and Instruction Retirement/Decoded Tick
algorithms.notes: Invalidation after 256 decoded instructions ensures only fresh, correlated values influence branch predictions.

algorithms.name: Predict (Lookup)
algorithms.trigger: Fetch / Lookup time when computing Statistical Corrector inputs
algorithms.notes: Bank output scaling by 2.5 (can be implemented via (bank_sum * 5) >> 1) applies per bank when the selected register has positive usefulness; otherwise the bank is masked (x0).

algorithms.name: Update (Training)
algorithms.notes: Single write-port per table: only one available register per bank is trained per branch event, chosen uniformly at random among available registers in that bank.

host_interfaces.need: In-flight destination register identifier and ROB tag at Decode
host_interfaces.description: The branch predictor needs to know when an in-flight instruction allocates a destination logical register, clearing the scoreboard valid bit and recording the ROB tag.
host_interfaces.fallback: If decode notifications are absent, track register updates at writeback/execution time only; register valid windows become smaller and post-mispredict boost is dampened.

host_interfaces.need: Completed register values from execution backend
host_interfaces.description: Functional unit execution units or common data bus must broadcast (ROB tag, dest register ID, 64-bit value, type) upon completing execution so digests can be written to the scoreboard.
host_interfaces.fallback: If execution broadcasts are unavailable, forward committed register values from the architectural register file at instruction commit.

host_interfaces.need: Pipeline squash / branch misprediction recovery notification
host_interfaces.description: Signals squash event and the squashed ROB tag boundary to restore speculative register scoreboard state.
host_interfaces.fallback: Clear all valid bits in the scoreboard on misprediction recovery, re-accumulating valid digests only as post-recovery instructions complete.

host_interfaces.description: Periodic or per-instruction pulse indicating decoded instructions to decrement the 8-bit aging decay counter.
host_interfaces.fallback: Decrement decay counter on branch lookup requests or cycle ticks if per-instruction decode pulses are not provided by the host.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: Prediction weight tables (WT): 6 bits * (128 + 256 + 512 entries) * 8 banks = 43,008 bits. Usefulness weight tables (UT): 6 bits * 65 registers * (8 + 8 + 8 entries) = 9,360 bits. Auxiliary register tracking table: 65 entries * (1 valid bit + 14 payload bits + 8 decay counter bits) = 1,495 bits. Total = 43,008 + 9,360 + 1,495 = 53,863 bits (6.57 KiB).
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: Requires 8 parallel search blocks to find maximum usefulness across available registers (up to 9 comparisons per bank), 12-bit digest generators (XOR-folds and bit-selects), and fixed-point scaling (* 2.5, implemented as (sum * 5) >> 1). Each table needs only 1 write port due to random single-register selection per bank.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: At iso-storage, tagged table entries or high-bank history entries in TAGE can be downsized (e.g., reducing high banks from 25 to 23 banks, or shaving base bimodal entries from 128K to 96K) to accommodate the 53,863 bits of sR.

parameters.name: num_banks
parameters.storage_impact: Directly scales WT storage and partitions the 65 logical registers across banks.

parameters.name: decay_threshold
parameters.storage_impact: Alters bit width of decay_ctr: ceil(log2(decay_threshold)) * num_registers

parameters.name: bank_useful_multiplier
parameters.storage_impact: 0 bits (arithmetic scaling constant in adder tree)

parameters.name: num_tracked_registers
parameters.storage_impact: Scales UT storage and auxiliary scoreboard storage linearly.

unit_tests.name: integer_digest_generation_check
unit_tests.given: Integer register with value 0x0000000000000008 (leading zeros = 60, trailing zeros = 3, LSB6 = 8).

unit_tests.name: scoreboard_aging_invalidation
unit_tests.given: Register R4 is valid with decay_ctr = 2. Advance decode tick by 2 instructions without execution updates to R4.
unit_tests.expect: R4 decay_ctr decrements to 1 then 0; R4.valid transitions to 0 (digest becomes invalid and unavailable for lookup).

unit_tests.name: usefulness_gated_scaling
unit_tests.given: Bank 0 has valid R0 with combined usefulness UT sum = +4 (> 0) and WT sum = 10. Bank 1 has no valid registers.
unit_tests.expect: Bank 0 contributes int(10 * 2.5) = 25 to sR_sum. Bank 1 contributes 0. Total contribution from these two banks is 25.

unit_tests.name: single_write_port_random_selection
unit_tests.given: Update triggered for branch where Bank 2 had registers R2 and R10 both valid at prediction time.
unit_tests.expect: Exactly one register from {R2, R10} is randomly chosen for WT/UT table update, requiring at most 1 write port per table.

open_questions: How does the hardware distinguish whether to count zeros or ones for the INT digest leading/trailing run-length fields (e.g., does it test bit 63 and bit 0 dynamically, or always count leading/trailing zeros)? Assumed: counts runs matching the MSB for leading and matching the LSB for trailing.

Exact format-detection logic for floating point registers (FP16 vs FP32 vs FP64) when inspecting most significant bits is not formalized in the paper. Assumed: ISA instruction opcode or register file descriptor specifies the active FP width.
Exact random replacement policy and pseudo-random seed generator during training when multiple registers in a bank are valid. Assumed: uses the global 64-bit PRNG specified in Table 2.
